title: UPCC v2.0 — Spine Schema (17-field minimal legitimate design)

title.description: Names the course so it can be referenced/cited. Elicit: "One-line course name?"

claim.description: States exactly what capability the course produces — the thing everything else must trace back to. Elicit: "In 1–2 sentences: this course helps the learner do/decide what?"

non_claims.description: Blocks overclaim by stating what the course does NOT produce (mandatory pairing with course.claim per §1). Elicit: "What should this course NOT be mistaken for claiming?"

situation.description: The real problem/change that makes this course necessary — the origin, not a topic. Elicit: "What real situation or breakdown is happening right now?"

purpose.description: The changed state the learner should return to the world with. Elicit: "If this works, how does the learner face that same situation differently afterward?"

prior_knowledge.description: What the learner already brings — prevents content dump / re-teaching known things. Elicit: "What do these learners already know or have done before, related to this problem?"

barriers.description: What blocks them now — language, access, time, confidence, etc. Elicit: "What's stopping them from acting on this already?"

working_words.description: The new lens/term that reframes the problem into an actionable question — the schema's anti-content-dump hinge. Elicit: "What single new term or lens would make them ask a different, more useful question about this?"

opens.description: What the term opens up (optional at spine depth).

changed_questions.description: Questions the term makes newly askable (optional at spine depth).

routes.description: Route ids this term feeds (optional at spine depth; full route objects live in top-level routes[]).

The concrete path from the new question to a tool/workflow/skill that can answer it. Elicit: "Given that new question, what domain/tool/workflow/skill actually answers it, and what counts as 'done right'?"

overall.description: The single outcome sentence — "learner can now ___". Elicit: "One sentence: what can the learner now do that they couldn't before?"

human_return.description: What the learner can do UNASSISTED — the proof the capability is theirs, not the AI's/teacher's. Elicit: "With help removed, what specifically can they still do on their own?"

must_know.description: The irreducible knowledge needed for the capability (not "interesting," needed). Elicit: "What must they know for the route above to work at all?"

must_do.description: The irreducible hands-on action — a skill needs doing it, not hearing about it. Elicit: "What must they actually DO, not just learn about?"

sessions.description: At least one concrete teaching unit that produces observable evidence, not just "covers content." Elicit: "In one session, how long, targeting which capability slice, what does the learner do, and what artifact/evidence results?"

assessment.description: UPCC's 6-field evidence chain — stops the course from asserting a capability it never checked. Elicit: "What will you claim they can do; what task shows it; what will you observe; what counts as enough; why does that observation support the claim; and how much help were they given while doing it?"

assistance_condition.description: The condition under which the task was performed (assisted vs. unassisted) — makes the 'assisted performance ≠ Human Return' discipline (§13, §15) checkable.

closure_pack.description: What the learner leaves with so the course can actually end (§19 closure discipline). Elicit: "What must they have in hand before this course is considered closed?"

single_return_if_needed.description: Whether one bounded follow-up touchpoint is needed — blocks open-ended, unbounded follow-up. Elicit: "Is one later check-in needed, or is this fully self-service after closure?"

delivery_mode.description: Optional. Primary delivery mode. ONLINE_SYNCHRONOUS (synchronous group videoconference) makes the toledo_h07 block mandatory and enforced by mcp/server.py validate_design. Values are exact, upper-case.

toledo_h07.description: Optional; required (and only allowed) when delivery_mode is ONLINE_SYNCHRONOUS. Design descriptions and evidence plans for the 9 ordered states of Toledo EQ-002/H.07.v1 (CAN-1318, tier Definition = composition, not a proved or validated causal law). Descriptions only: no numbers, probabilities, scores or predicted learner outcomes. Rules beyond JSON Schema (order, forbidden inferences, endorser, assistance) are enforced heuristically by mcp/server.py validate_design.

stages.description: Exactly 9 stages in canonical order: ZoomState -> Barrier -> CandidateRoute -> LiveRoute -> HumanReturn -> ReturnDelta -> LiveField -> RealizedOpportunity -> NetAdvancement.

design.description: How this state is designed/read in this course (description, not a number).

evidence_basis.description: Kinds of evidence planned. camera_on/attendance/session_duration/chat_volume/poll_response are platform traces: allowed for ZoomState and Barrier only; on every other stage trace-only evidence (or a plan that mentions traces without a performance-type kind) is rejected by mcp/server.py. Required for HumanReturn, ReturnDelta, RealizedOpportunity, NetAdvancement, and on those four it must include a performance-type kind: unaided_task_performance, delayed_unaided_task, work_product_review or human_observation.

evidence_plan.description: Prose plan for how the evidence will be gathered.

endorser.description: LiveRoute only, required there: the human who chooses the route. An AI/system suggestion is not a human choice.

assistance_condition.description: HumanReturn only, required there: must be unassisted; assisted performance is not unaided Human Return.
